lantern_21_061.text: Her private notebook held three completed great circuits on three recovered dates, each followed by a distinct stopped initiation and normal next-day condition. It also held the prior practice, real failure, and qualified recovery that made the later series possible. The pages did not promise personal flight, a liquid reservoir, another dantian, or fuel for six settlements. They described an earned bounded task whose final received title still lay ahead. Yue put the notebook on the high shelf and chose an ordinary evening with people who knew more about her than its measurements.

lantern_21_062.speaker: narrator
lantern_21_062.text: On the last evening of the period Gao brought his apprentice's later bowl to a visit. Its glaze still ran at one edge, and its intended household use could accept that flaw. Lo had chosen the smaller lawful purpose rather than selling it as the flawless ordered piece. Gao wanted Yue to admire it because he had finally praised a particular improvement without turning praise into acceptance of every condition. She did. The bowl stood cold on their table, useful and honestly imperfect.

lantern_21_063.speaker: narrator
lantern_21_063.text: Tian filled it with thread ends she had already bought, while the boy wanted to test whether a paper bird could sit inside. Its clay owner allowed the game and received it back before leaving. Yue noticed how many useful small visits ended by returning the object. The next recipient would not need to reconstruct custody from a story of everyone's kindness. Gao put the bowl in its dry wrapping and carried it home after the agreed hour.

lantern_21_064.speaker: narrator
lantern_21_064.text: The visit left no new employment, no hidden reference fuel, and no extra examination result in Yue's account. It left a pleasant memory and a clearer picture of an apprentice's choice. A pleasant visit could matter on its own. Yue wrote no lesson for public circulation that night. She washed her own bowl, placed it where Tian could reach the table, and let the room contain silence once the boy had fallen asleep beside his toys.

lantern_21_065.speaker: narrator
lantern_21_065.text: Her review would arrive on its actual date. Until then the completed course remained completed evidence, the expected certificate remained unissued, and the town's two-window service continued under its real paid roster. Yue extinguished the lamp at the household's agreed hour. Somewhere along the return road Fang still carried the admitted bag. Somewhere farther away her mother had moved a chair nearer a kitchen window. Neither place came closer through an unfinished title, and both could be reached only by real later travel or correspondence.
